review.summary:
Lens: user surface and UX, round 2, on tree 969a8e5. I ran target/debug/planroom on copies of the built fixture (/tmp/planroom-e2e-*/shop copied into my scratchpad, with PLANROOM_DATA in the scratchpad). I read every PNG in docs/screenshots, plus the canvas shell/views/store/transport, the mod's layout.ts, register.tsx, room.ts, fallback.ts and engine.ts, en.toml, cli.rs and the resolver. I could not run the mod host or a browser, so mod and canvas behaviour comes from reading the code, and each finding says which parts I verified.

Round-1 material fix check:
- ux-1 HOLDS. Block rows are plain text with no row key (layout.ts:279-317). A pressed next action stores `shown` and draws its result with a "Back to the … level" press (layout.ts:155-185, register.tsx:216-260). One odd case is in ux-a below.
- ux-2 HOLDS. Verified: the envelope carries `summary` (for example `map --json` gives "10 at the top: kit (11 code, …"). roomText returns the summary plus at most 3 handles, never JSON (room.ts:138-147). A gap remains for truncated maps (ux-e).
- ux-3 HOLDS for blankness. Verified: `map --level intent` returns `empty.reason=no_intent`, and the canvas draws LevelEmpty for a zero-node map (map-view.tsx:185-215). But the merged engine's label makes that screen say the same thing twice, and the screenshot doesn't show it (ux-d).
- ux-4 HOLDS. Breadcrumbs now follow the level (levels.ts crumbsAt), the phone has a ⋯ lid, and the next action becomes "Back to shop" (container-390x844 screenshots). But the ⋯ lid's tap area is 34 px (ux-b).
- ux-6 HOLDS. Verified in an empty dir: `focus` and `map` both return ok with `no_repos`, and the next action is `focus`. But the same failing-scan loop comes back for a repo with no commits (ux-c).

Known minor gaps that are unchanged and not re-reported: ux-7 (the `e` key and the login path), ux-8 (the Artifact's "Ask your computer" while it can't), ux-9 (hints dropped, full-page takeover), ux-10 (hard-coded mod strings), ux-11 (no tones, truncated subtitles), ux-12 (jargon such as "moved" and "at the top" at every level), and unasked-9 (plurals such as "Map these 1 repos").

New problems in brief:
- A single uncommitted repo blocks the whole workspace and loops the one next action. This is material and verified.
- The phone's way back up has a 34 px target, and the 44 px gate never visits that state. Material, verified from the screenshot pixels and the CSS.
- "No project" opens a blank sheet. Material per the "never a blank state" principle, verified from the code.
- `Empty` has one string doing double duty as the line and the button.
- The screenshots predate the ENGINE merge.
- The next action never changes with level.
- The rail's System step shows a different map from the top-level map, with the same name.
- Usage errors lose the missing argument's name. Verified with `share --json`.
- `/room` hides truncation.
- `/room share` gives the model no publish arguments.
- "Check again" during a source build offers a second, clobbering build. Read only, not run.
- The fix page and some hints can't be followed where the person is.

findings.title: One repo with no commits blocks the whole workspace: scan fails, and every surface keeps offering that same scan as the next action
findings.evidence: Verified. I copied the fixture, added `newsvc/` with `git init` and no commit, then ran `planroom scan --json`. The reply is `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"git_failed","retry":"never","message":"git failed in newsvc: fatal: Needed a single revision","hint":null,...}}`, exit 8. `planroom focus` afterwards still prints "Map these 6 repos? About 2 s." with next = `scan <root>`. With only an unborn repo (`w/bare/r1`), the same happens: scan exits 8 and focus offers the same scan again. The other 5 repos get no map at all. The pre-fix tree used the same `rev-parse --verify HEAD^{commit}` (`git grep` at 6cc222d), so the SCAN fix didn't introduce this, but it is the same loop ux-6 was rated material for. The mod's band key `1`, the pane's Next button and the canvas's top empty state would each run the failing scan again; for those three I assumed the behaviour from layout.ts:445-468 and app.tsx:44-56 and did not run them.
findings.why: This breaks the KICKOFF principle "Never show a blank state" and R1's "no repo gets nothing": a `git init` for a new service is an everyday workspace state, and it leaves every repo unmapped. The only next action is a scan that fails, and its raw git error has no hint and `retry: never`. It is the same shape as material finding ux-6.
findings.fix: Have discovery or scan skip a repo with an unborn HEAD and add a warning naming it ("newsvc has no commits yet; it maps after its first commit"), so the rest of the workspace still maps. Until then, give git_failed a hint, and don't offer `scan` as focus's next action when the last scan failed this way.

findings.title: On the phone, the ⋯ lid (the way back up) has a 34 px tap area, and the 44 px e2e check never visits a level where that lid exists
findings.evidence: Verified from the screenshot pixels. In container-390x844-light.png (2x), dark border columns sit at x=32-35 (the ⋯ lid's left edge) and at x=100-103 (the current lid's left edge) on rows 60, 74 and 100. That leaves 68 device px, or 34 CSS px, of exposed ⋯ target. The CSS explains it: the ⋯ button is `.lid-ancestor` with `margin-right: -10px` and `min-width: var(--target)` (44 px), and `.lid-current` is `position: relative`, so it paints over the last 10 px and takes their hits. The e2e test `the_top_row_holds_four_targets_at_most_every_target_is_44px...` measures each button's boundingBox only after `openMap`, at the top level, where the ⋯ lid isn't rendered (surface.spec.ts:425-427 asserts it has count 0 there). The overlap is therefore never measured.
findings.why: S13 (tier B) and design-language.md "Touch" require every target on the phone to be at least 44 px. This lid is the gesture table's way back up, "Tap the ⋯ lid, then an ancestor".
findings.fix: Drop the negative margin on `.lid-more` (or give `.lid-more` a 10 px right padding so its exposed part is 44 px). Extend the 44 px test to run again after "Open the containers", and measure hit-testable width with `elementFromPoint`, not boundingBox.

findings.title: The project shelf's "No project" chip opens a blank sheet; the lens switcher opens a one-entry sheet that does nothing
findings.evidence: Verified by reading the code. With `pane.focus.project === null` (true on the fixture: `focus --json` gives `"project": null`), TopRow passes `entries={[]}` to Picker. A press sets `open`, and Picker renders `.picker-sheet.panel` (min-width 200px, padding 6px, border) around an empty `<ul>`: an empty box with no line and no action. The lens Picker has one entry and no `onPick`, so a press on "all" closes the sheet and does nothing. On the phone the chip is one of the top row's four targets (main-390x844 screenshots).
findings.why: KICKOFF principle 1 says "Never show a blank state", and S15 requires that an empty-state audit finds none. design-language.md "Empty states" also asks for the felt with one block waiting and the single next action.
findings.fix: With no projects, draw the sheet as an EmptyState with one line and its next action (for now a line such as "No projects yet"), or make the chip non-interactive until M1. Hide the lens sheet when it has a single entry.

findings.title: An Empty's one label is used as both the line and the button: the intent level says the same thing twice, no_repos becomes a 104-character button the pane cuts mid-sentence, and pressing "check again" leaves a meaningless Back press
findings.evidence: Verified. `map --level intent --detail graph --json` gives `empty.next.label = "No plans at the intent level yet. Show the top of the map."`. LevelEmpty draws `line = "Nothing at the intent level yet."` and, because `next !== null`, a button carrying that whole two-sentence label. Verified: `focus --json` in an empty dir gives a 104-character label, "No git repos here. Open Planroom in a folder that holds your repos, or clone one here, then check again.". The canvas's top-level empty state draws only that as a button, with no line (app.tsx:47-55). The pane cuts it to `columns-3` = 46 columns, "No git repos here. Open Planroom in a folder …" (computed with ui truncate), so the instruction and "check again" are lost. I read but did not run what follows. After a press, `shown` matches (same command, same seq 0), so the card shows the label twice and a "Back to the system level" button. With no store there is no watch loop to refresh the pane, so after cloning a repo the person must press Back, then the button again.
findings.why: This makes an empty-state decision costlier than it needs to be, against principle 1. Each empty state should show one line and one short next action.
findings.fix: Give `Empty` an optional `line` next to `next` (additive), split the [empty] strings into a line and a short label ("Show the top of the map", "Check again"), have surfaces draw the line as text, and don't keep `shown` for a `focus` press.

findings.title: docs/screenshots predate the ENGINE merge, so they show labels and states the merged tree doesn't produce
findings.evidence: Verified with git. The screenshots were last written at 2a4897b (the SURFACES track, 13:28). `git merge-base --is-ancestor c475b36 2a4897b` gives `no`, so the ENGINE commit that added the `no_intent`, `empty_level` and `nothing_mapped` Empties isn't in them. No screenshot commit follows the merges 687c713 and e700ebc, or 744976a (`git log -- docs/screenshots` gives only 2a4897b). empty-level-1440x900-dark.png shows the fallback button "Back to shop", but against the merged engine LevelEmpty takes the engine's label (ux-d). The empty-*.png files date from 09:58, before every fix, and come from the stand-in.
findings.why: S15's empty-state screenshot audit and this review read these images as the product's states, and they don't match the merged tree.
findings.fix: Rerun `cargo xtask e2e --screens` on the merged tree, and add a check that the screenshots' commit is not older than the last change under packages/canvas or crates/planroom/text.

findings.title: The pane's next action is always "Open the containers", whatever the level or the map
findings.evidence: Verified: focus.rs sets `level: Level::System` and next = `map --level container` with `focus.next_containers`, unconditionally. I verified one case end to end: on a workspace with one repo and an empty commit, `focus` gives "Next: Open the containers" and `map --level container` gives "Nothing at the container level here. Show the top of the map.", whose way back returns to the same press, so there is no real next action. The rest I read but did not run: on the canvas at component or code level, alreadyShown is false, so the card says "Open the containers" but goes up a level. At intent the card stack keeps "Open the containers" next to the empty state's own button, giving two primary actions on one screen (empty-level screenshot).
findings.why: S1 asks for "one suggested next action", and principle 1 asks to respect attention. This one is mislabelled at some levels and a dead end on small workspaces.
findings.fix: Have the canvas hide the pane's next action on a level other than the pane's own (or below container), and have focus offer `map --level container` only when that level has blocks.

findings.title: The rail's System step and the top lid name the same place but show different maps, and the rail draws Intent nested above System
findings.evidence: Verified: `map --detail graph` returns 10 nodes, while `map --level system --detail graph` returns 5 (kit, orders, platform, storefront, worker); the 5 externals drop out. At the top the rail marks System current (`s.level ?? s.map?.level`), and pressing it sets level "system". crumbsAt('system') returns only the top lid, so the breadcrumb still reads "shop" while 5 blocks vanish. On the Artifact, viewKey maps level "system" to `map:system:all`, the top map, so the same press shows 10 there. The rail lists Intent first, joined to System by the level line (screenshots), but DR-85 says intent "sits beside the system level". This is engine drift-6 made visible, and the ux-4 fix made it worse by giving the two views the same name.
findings.why: Levels are one of the five ideas: the same named place showing two different contents, and differing between surfaces, undermines "where I am".
findings.fix: Have the rail's System step call `back()` (the top map) until drift-6 is fixed, and draw Intent apart from the System to Code chain.

findings.title: A usage error's message drops the missing argument ("…were not provided:."), and `/room share`, which /room help offers, hits it
findings.evidence: Verified: `planroom share --json` gives `"message":"The command line isn't valid: the following required arguments were not provided:."`. cli.rs takes only `rendered.lines().next()`, and clap puts the missing `--out <OUT>` on the next line. `details.field` is "out", but the one line a person reads names nothing. `share` is `room: true`, so `/room share` (architecture.md:248 and 1397) runs this exact line and fails. The mod then toasts the message with a CLI hint, `planroom schema --command share`, inside /room.
findings.why: en.toml rules say messages are one engine-authored, actionable line. This one is broken, and the documented `/room share` fails on first use.
findings.fix: For MissingRequiredArgument, build `why` from clap's ContextKind::InvalidArg ("--out is required"). Give share a default `--out .planroom/share`, as architecture.md:1397 says.

findings.title: /room hides a truncated map: the summary counts blocks the result doesn't hold, and the drill-down handle never reaches the person or the model
findings.evidence: Verified: `map --level code --json` has summary "83 at the top: …; and 71 more." and 22 nodes, with the drill-down only in `meta.warnings[0].details.next` (`map --level component`). I read but did not run the mod side. handlesOf reads `meta.next`, `result.empty.next` and `result.next`, never `meta.warnings`. roomText therefore returns the summary with no handle, and roomRows draws 22 block rows with no warning row and no "+61 more" (that row only appears past 200 nodes).
findings.why: Principle 2 asks for summary-first answers "with handles to drill down", and DR-85 has the truncated warning name a drill-down that runs today. /room drops it, so the person sees 83 promised and 22 drawn.
findings.fix: In handlesOf, also collect `meta.warnings[*].details.next`, and in roomRows add a dim row with the warning's message when `meta.truncated` is set.

findings.title: `/room share` returns no publish arguments to the model, so the documented publish can't follow it
findings.evidence: Read, not run in the mod. Architecture.md:1397 says "/room share … returns `context` with the exact publish arguments: file_path, files, capabilities…". The command.run handler returns only `{ text: roomText(...) }`, and roomText is the summary plus handles. Verified: share's result has `publish` (file_path and files) but no handle, so the model reads only "Shares 5 repos, 10 blocks …; no code text; no presence.". The publish args are drawn only as JSON in CommandOutput, for the person. DR-85's "never JSON" text rule leaves no channel for them. WS7 used the CLI directly, so nothing exercised this path.
findings.why: This is a design gap the ux-2 fix exposed: the person path to S11's publish (architecture.md:248, "the chat model makes the one publish call") can't complete from what the model is given.
findings.fix: Return share's publish arguments in the command result's `context` field (or as a handle the model can act on), and record that exception to the summary-only text rule in DR-85.

findings.title: During a source build, the fallback's only button ("Check again", also band key 1) flips the pane back to "Build it", and a second press starts a build that deletes the first one's clone
findings.evidence: Read, not run. The building pane's action is "Check again" (run: retry), which calls startEngine and runs `resolver version --json`. The resolver has no idea a build is in progress: build() takes no lock, and resolve() goes straight to `offer_build` with reason no_release, no_build or download_failed. engineFromVersion maps that to `build_offered`, so the pane and band offer "Build it" while the first build is still running. A second build runs `rm -rf "$src"` and clones into the directory the first `cargo build` is using (installed-plugin path). When the first build fails, act() then sets status `failed`.
findings.why: Here the one obvious next action makes things worse, during a 4-minute wait the pane says to expect.
findings.fix: Give `build` a lock (reuse the fetch lock) and have resolve report `engine_fetching` ("a build is running") while it's held. Or have the pane's building state offer no action until act()'s build returns.

findings.title: Some fix lines and hints can't be run from where the person is, and the no-canvas fix page is a bare white page
findings.evidence:
Verified by reading. `hint.engine_unavailable = "scripts/planroom build"` and `canvas.missing_install = "…then run scripts/planroom build."` are paths relative to the plugin's install directory, which a person in their workspace doesn't know. The resolver itself prints the absolute `$self build` (planroom:350-352), so the engine's strings disagree with it. fix_page() writes `

…

…` with no styles, so the browser's white default background shows. design-language.md lists "A cream or off-white background" under Don't, and asks every empty state for the felt with one next action. git_failed (ux-a) has no hint at all.
findings.why: AGENTS.md says hints are exact commands. These can't be run as written, and the page breaks the design language.
findings.fix: Interpolate the resolver's absolute path (the engine can read it from engine.env or PLANROOM_RESOLVER), or say "/plugin" steps. Give the fix page the --table and --card tokens and the empty-state art.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced with target/debug/planroom on a temp workspace (svc1, svc2 with one commit each, newsvc after `git init` only, PLANROOM_DATA in scratch). `scan --json` gave `{ok:false, code:git_failed, retry:never, message:"git failed in newsvc: fatal: Needed a single revision", hint:null}`. Then `focus --json` gave next = `scan <root>` with the label "Map these 3 repos? About 2 s." and empty.reason not_scanned, so the two healthy repos got no map and the only next action is the same failing scan. Source: crates/extract/src/git.rs:86 runs `rev-parse --verify HEAD^{commit}` with no handling for an unborn HEAD. en.toml [hint] has no git_failed entry. The README and DR-85 don't log the case. This breaks KICKOFF principle 1 ("Never show a blank state") and R1's "no repo gets nothing", so material stands. I did not run the surface half (mod key 1, canvas empty state); it is inferred from code.

Confirmed from CSS and pixels. The phone's ⋯ lid is a Picker with className lid-more and buttonClass `lid lid-ancestor lid-more-button` (top-row.tsx:36-49). `.lid-ancestor` has `margin-right:-10px` (styles.css:215-218), so the button overflows its `.picker` wrapper by 10px. The next flex item `.lid-current` is `position:relative` (styles.css:244-248) and later in DOM order, so it paints over that 10px and takes its hits. In container-390x844-light.png (2x), dark border columns sit at x=32-35 and x=100-103 on rows 60, 74 and 100, which leaves 68 device px, or 34 CSS px, exposed. The e2e test at surface.spec.ts:380-401 checks boundingBox only after openMap at the top level, where the ⋯ lid is absent (asserted at :425-427). S13 is tier B (KICKOFF:128,184) and requires 44 px targets, so material stands.

Confirmed in code. TopRow (top-row.tsx:174-186) passes `entries=[]` to the project Picker whenever pane.focus.project is null, and focus.rs:63-70 always sets project None. A press sets open, and Picker (picker.tsx:64-90) renders `.picker-sheet.panel` around an empty <ul>, styled min-width 200px with a border (styles.css:388+). That is an empty box with no line and no action, a blank state under KICKOFF principle 1, so material holds for the project shelf. The lens half (one entry, no onPick) is only a no-op and would on its own be minor. Neither case is logged as a known gap in the README or DR-85.

Confirmed. On a scanned temp workspace, `map --level intent --detail graph --json` gives empty.next.label "No plans at the intent level yet. Show the top of the map.". LevelEmpty (map-view.tsx:185-206) draws STRINGS.emptyLevel as the line plus a button with that whole label, so the text repeats. In an empty dir, `focus --json` gives the 104-character no_repos label. app.tsx:47-55 draws only that label as the button, and layout.ts:189 cuts it to columns-3. Envelope `Empty` has only reason and next (envelope.rs:221-224). This is a UX cost, not a blank state, so minor is right.

Confirmed with git. `git log -- docs/screenshots` shows 2a4897b (13:28) as the last write. `git merge-base --is-ancestor c475b36 2a4897b` gives no. Commits 744976a, 687c713, e700ebc and c475b36 changed packages/canvas or crates/planroom/text after it. The screenshots therefore predate the engine's empty-state labels. This is drift in evidence, not product behaviour, so minor.

Confirmed. focus.rs:63-82 sets next = `map --level container` with focus.next_containers unconditionally, at level System. On a 2-repo temp workspace, `focus` gave "Open the containers", and `map --level container --json` gave empty_level with "Nothing at the container level here. Show the top of the map.", so that press is a dead end. next-action.ts:26-41 only swaps in Back when the level already matches. This is a mislabel or loop at the edges, not a blank state, so minor.

Confirmed in code. ZoomRail (zoom-rail.tsx:13) marks `s.level ?? s.map?.level` as current, so at the top (level null, map.level system) System is marked, and a press calls showLevel('system'), which is `map --level system`. That map drops blocks, per drift-6 (README:64, logged as a minor known gap). artifact.ts:97-100 maps level system to `map:system:all`, the top view, so the two surfaces differ. I did not rerun the 10-vs-5 node count, because the fixture isn't built here. This is the UI face of a logged minor gap, so it stays minor.

Reproduced. `planroom share --json` gave message "The command line isn't valid: the following required arguments were not provided:." with details.field "out". cli.rs:265 takes only `rendered.lines().next()`, and clap puts the missing argument on the next line. The generated catalogue marks share `room: true`, and the /room run handler (register.tsx:507-517) passes the person's args through unchanged, adding no default --out, so a bare `/room share` fails this way. The synopsis and the schema hint still name --out, so it's recoverable. Minor.

Confirmed in code. handlesOf (room.ts:94-110) reads meta.next, result.empty.next and result.next, never meta.warnings. roomRows adds the '+N more' row only past 200 nodes and has no warning row. map.rs:5,140-160 puts the drill-down in the truncated warning's details.next. I did not rerun the 83/22 numbers, because the fixture isn't built. The person still sees the summary, so minor.

Confirmed. The /room run case returns only `{ text: roomText(...) }` (register.tsx:520-528), and roomText is the summary plus handles. On a temp workspace, `share --out DIR --json` has summary "Shares 2 repos, ...; no code text; no presence.", meta.next None, and the publish args only in result.publish. So the model gets no file_path or files, against architecture.md:1397. The model can still list the --out directory, so S11 isn't certain to fail. Minor design gap.

Confirmed by reading. The building fallback uses action "Check again" with run retry (fallback.ts:55-56, en.toml:83-85). build() in plugin/scripts/planroom:374-398 does `rm -rf "$src"` and clones without take_lock, which only the download path takes (planroom:257). While the build runs, resolve has no engine and goes to offer_build, so engineFromVersion maps no_build to build_offered (engine.ts:136-138). A second Build press could therefore clobber the first clone. I did not run it. It needs two presses during a rare source build, so minor.

Confirmed. en.toml:28 has `hint.engine_unavailable = "scripts/planroom build"`, and en.toml:121 has missing_install "...run scripts/planroom build.", both relative paths. The resolver itself prints the absolute `$self build` (planroom:350-352). The en.toml comment says these are fallbacks used only when the resolver gives no line, which limits their reach. fix_page (canvas.rs:59-66) is unstyled HTML on the browser's default white, against design-language.md:26,134. Minor.
